name: Dijkstra's Algorithm
description: Finds shortest paths from a source vertex to all other vertices in a weighted graph with non-negative edge weights. Uses a greedy approach with a min-priority queue.
aim: Find shortest distances from source to all vertices by greedily selecting the unvisited vertex with minimum distance, then relaxing its neighbors.
howItWorks: Add source to min-priority queue with priority 0
Extract vertex with minimum distance (greedy choice)
For each neighbor: if dist[u]+weight < dist[v], update dist[v]
Add updated neighbors to priority queue
Repeat until queue empty — all shortest paths found

time.worstCase: Dense graph with simple array priority queue

complexity.spaceDescription: Distance array + priority queue hold at most V elements

realWorld: Video games — NPC pathfinding on weighted grids
whenToUse: Single-source shortest path in weighted graph
Finding shortest path in road/network maps
alternatives: Floyd-Warshall — when all-pairs shortest paths needed
A* — when heuristic available for target-specific search
